findings.how_to_check: Run `replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do` and compare `valGainTarget` (28%) with `valGainAncTarget` (16.0%) and `valGainFsTarget` (11.5%). In Stata on `temp.dta`, tabulate `validated_before validated_after if linked_before==1 & linked_after==1 & id_A_before==id_A_after`: 165,580 kept records change validation status solely because mi1940 changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not revert create_figures_SSHA2025.do to own-file middle initials. Retain one fixed 1940 middle initial (Ancestry or FamilySearch) across both before and after link files, and update the paper text (lines 68, 98, 548) and Table 4 to report the true fixed-validator gain (16.0% under Ancestry, 11.5% under FamilySearch). If the 28% moving figure is retained in an appendix, explicitly describe it as conflating link changes with middle-initial transcription changes rather than 'match quality'.
findings.title: Reintroducing a moving 1940 middle-initial validator invalidates the headline 28% match-quality improvement claim
findings.what_the_code_does: CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:70-86 reverts the 2026-11-01 fix, redefining `validated_before = mi`beg_yr'==mi1940` using mi1940 from the Ancestry link file, and `validated_after = mi`beg_yr'==mi1940` using mi1940 from the ML model link file. The expression `100*((sv_after/sv_before)-1)` in line 211 computes the percentage change when both the link partner and the 1940 evaluation standard change simultaneously.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper's Abstract (line 68), Introduction (line 98), and main results (lines 547-549) claim a 28% increase in match quality (65% to 84%) on discordant records, arguing that recovered links are true rather than spurious. When the validator is held fixed, the true link-quality gain is only 16.0% (Ancestry initial) or 11.5% (FamilySearch initial). For 829,471 kept target links pairing the exact same individuals, validation jumps from 63.4% to 79.2% solely because the 1940 initial was re-transcribed. Reverting to the moving validator produces an inflated number that fails like-for-like comparison.

findings.how_to_check: In Stata, inspect `v_cf` on switched links: `count if status==2 & v_cf != validated_after` returns 0. Compare `v_cf` with a true fixed-initial counterfactual `mi1930_after == mi1940_anc` for `status==2`: the two differ, proving that `ppLinks` absorbs the validator shift on switched links.
findings.suggested_fix: Construct the counterfactual validation flag using a constant 1940 middle initial (e.g. Ancestry's `mi1940_anc`) across all link categories: for after links, evaluate `mi1930_new == mi1940_fixed` for both kept (status==1) and switched (status==2) links. Decompose relative to that fixed baseline, and account for denominator attrition from missing initials.
findings.title: Counterfactual in new validation decomposition misclassifies validator shifts on switched links as linkage effects
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 93-94 define `gen byte v_cf = validated_after if linked_after==1` and `replace v_cf = validated_before if status==1`. For switched links (`status==2`), `v_cf` retains `validated_after` (which uses the new model's 1940 initial). The code then defines `ppLinks = 100*(cf - b)` as the effect of 'which links exist' and `ppRescoring = 100*(a - cf)` as the effect of rescoring. For all switched links, `a - cf` is identically 0.
findings.why_it_matters: The new decomposition claims to separate linkage composition from validator rescoring. Because `v_cf` is not adjusted for switched links (16,435 records in the target group where validation moves from 33.6% to 75.1%), all rescoring of switched links is attributed to the link-existence component `ppLinks`. Furthermore, because `summarize` omits missing initials and initial availability shifts between versions (21,925 gained vs 71,780 lost on kept records), the decomposition operates over shifting denominators.

findings.how_to_check: Run `python replication/check_claims.py` in `D:/repos/fixing_transcription_errors`. Under the uncommitted diff, all claims report `MATCH` (50 match, 0 assert failures). Inspect `replication/claims_report.md:17-19` to see that `intro-val-gain`, `results-validated`, and `results-all` previously failed assertions against `valGainAncTarget` and `valGainFsTarget`.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the assertions `assert = "abs(valGainTarget - valGainAncTarget) < 0.05"` and `abs(valGainAll - valGainAncAll) < 0.05` in `replication/claims.toml` along with their explanatory notes. Retain the assert in `validation_fixed_initials.do`. Keep the replication check failing until the underlying analysis script and paper draft are updated to use consistent fixed-initial metrics.
findings.title: Claims registry assertions and diagnostic guards deleted to suppress replication failures on moving-validator claims
findings.what_the_code_does: The uncommitted diff in `replication/claims.toml` deletes the `assert = "abs(valGainTarget - valGainAncTarget) < 0.05"` and `abs(valGainAll - valGainAncAll) < 0.05` lines for claims `intro-val-gain`, `results-validated`, and `results-all`, and removes lines 80-91 of `replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do` which checked that `temp.dta` matched the fixed Ancestry validator.
findings.why_it_matters: Deleting these assertions masks the divergence between the paper's headline 28% and 1% validation claims and the fixed-validator diagnostic. Running `check_claims.py` produces a false clean bill of health (50 MATCH, 0 failures) without fixing the underlying measurement error. The replication guard was designed to prevent publishing contaminated statistics, and deleting the guard disables that protection.

review_limits: The analysis microdata (temp.dta, link1930_1940_*.dta) reside outside the repository and are gitignored; runtime Stata scripts could not be executed during this review.

The uncommitted decomposition outputs (ppLinks*, ppRescoring*) have not yet been written to `replication/results/validation_by_link_status.tex`; review of that logic was conducted via static code tracing.

Without ground-truth hand-transcribed names, this review can establish that the 28% statistic is sensitive to validator movement, but cannot establish which human transcription (Ancestry or FamilySearch) represents the ground truth.
Scope was limited to the working tree diff and the paper draft sections directly tied to it; untouched upstream linkage generation scripts were not re-audited.
structured_output.summary: The uncommitted changes reintroduce a moving 1940 middle-initial validator, causing the paper's headline 28 percent match-quality gain to conflate link changes with changes in how initials were transcribed. When evaluated against a fixed validator, the target-sample gain is substantially lower (16.0 percent under Ancestry, 11.5 percent under FamilySearch). The working tree also deletes the claims registry assertions that caught this discrepancy, and adds a decomposition that misallocates switched-link rescoring into the linkage-composition component.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
